overview: This file consists of five Department of State “List of Papers” index sheets summarizing records filed under newspapers and the press in Japan from 1940 through early 1944. The entries trace the contraction of the foreign-owned English-language press in wartime Japan—especially the pressured sales of the Japan Advertiser and Japan Chronicle and attempts to purchase or obstruct the Japan News-Week—along with censorship, propaganda, press attitudes toward the United States, and Japanese-language or Japanese-sponsored publications abroad. Several entries are cross-references to related files concerning South Africa, Argentina, Turkey, presidential cartoons, Axis activity, and overseas Japanese organizations.

subfiles.title: List of Papers: English-language press in Tokyo, item 66
subfiles.about: An index entry identifies a 1940 despatch concerning the English-language press in Tokyo and an enclosed Japan Times article.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records item 66, a despatch from Japan dated March 13, 1940, furnishing information about the English-language press in Tokyo. It notes the enclosure of an article published in the Japan Times on January 10. The form itself bears the later administrative date October 12, 1945.

subfiles.title: List of Papers sheet 8: Sales and pressure on foreign-owned newspapers
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes reports on the disposal of the Japan Advertiser and Japan Chronicle and attempts to acquire or undermine the Japan News-Week.
subfiles.summary: Entries record Benjamin W. Fleisher's wish to sell the Japan Advertiser, its eventual sale to the Japan Times under threat of confiscation, and the resulting suspension of State Department press releases to it. They also cover the sale of the British Japan Chronicle to Japanese interests and its anticipated continuation as an evening paper in Kobe. Later entries describe the American-owned Japan News-Week, an unsuccessful purchase offer from the Japan Information Bureau, alleged indirect sabotage, and a proposal to support the paper through advertising.

subfiles.title: List of Papers sheet 9: Press opinion, censorship, and cross-references
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes Japanese press reactions to American policy and wartime developments, together with related cross-references concerning South Africa and Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Several entries concern Japan News-Week editorials supporting American international policy and commenting on Roosevelt's March 15 speech and the Tripartite alliance. Another reports that editor W. R. Willis was censored for alleged anti-German material, although the Japanese Navy and Information Bureau reportedly valued his newspaper as a channel for Japanese-American relations. The sheet also summarizes vernacular coverage of expanded American patrol zones, Lindbergh, and trans-Siberian munitions shipments, while cross-referencing a naval-attaché controversy in South Africa, an unfavorable Roosevelt cartoon, and Hugo Fernández Artucio's statement about German and Axis activity in Argentina.

subfiles.title: List of Papers sheet 10: Japanese-American publications and overseas press material
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes comparative, censorship, propaganda, and overseas-publication records involving Japanese and Japanese-American newspapers.
subfiles.summary: The entries include a comparison of English- and Japanese-language Japanese-American newspapers and a report on Japanese objections to an anti-Nazi article in an American-owned paper. A memorandum attaches Thomas Millard's allegation that Matsuoka was purchasing newspapers for propaganda, while other entries concern a publication of the Overseas Japanese Central Society and a copy of JA-AE News Week sent to Mrs. Max Johnson Farmer. The later entries refer to letters from children in Japan and Japanese publications circulating in Argentina.

subfiles.title: List of Papers page 11: Japanese press in Argentina and Domei bulletins in Turkey
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes reports and enclosures concerning Japanese publications in Argentina and Domei News Bulletin issues distributed in Turkey.
subfiles.summary: One entry records a Justice Department report on Japanese publications in Argentina. Other entries cover copies of the Domei News Bulletin in Turkey, translations from the Japanese press of Buenos Aires for November 1–4, 1943, and further Japanese press reports. A January 1944 despatch analyzes the Argentine Japanese press's coverage of international news during November and December 1943, followed by a February response concerning the transmitted Domei bulletins.

interest: These index sheets offer a compact chronology of how Japan's remaining foreign-owned English-language newspapers were purchased, pressured, censored, or indirectly obstructed as wartime controls tightened. They are especially useful for tracing the disappearance of the Japan Advertiser and Japan Chronicle and the precarious survival of W. R. Willis's Japan News-Week, including official recognition of newspapers as channels in Japanese-American relations. The later sheets broaden the subject beyond Japan, revealing State Department interest in Japanese diaspora media, Domei material, and propaganda networks in Argentina and Turkey; the cross-references also help historians locate related records filed elsewhere in the decimal system.
